description: This topic explains who a consumer is, the rights and responsibilities of consumers, how consumers are exploited, and the ways and bodies used to protect consumers in Tanzania.

options.text: A person who manufactures goods for sale
A person who buys and uses goods and services to satisfy needs
A person who transports goods to the market
A person who advertises goods on television

mcq.explanation: A consumer is the final user who buys goods and services in order to satisfy his or her wants.

mcq.questionText: Selling goods at a price higher than the correct or agreed price is called

options.text: overcharging
adulteration
discounting
bargaining

mcq.explanation: Overcharging is a form of consumer exploitation where the trader charges more than the fair price.

mcq.questionText: Mixing a good quality product with a cheaper or harmful substance to increase quantity is known as

options.text: branding
adulteration
packaging
hoarding

mcq.explanation: Adulteration means adding inferior or harmful materials to genuine goods, for example mixing water with milk.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a right of a consumer?

options.text: The right to pay any price the seller demands
The right to be sold expired goods
The right to safety from harmful products
The right to avoid paying for goods bought

mcq.explanation: The right to safety protects consumers from goods and services that are dangerous to health and life.

mcq.questionText: Using a scale that shows more weight than the actual quantity given to a buyer is an example of

options.text: fair trading
false weights and measures
quality control
after-sales service

mcq.explanation: Using false weights and measures cheats the consumer by giving less than what is paid for.

mcq.questionText: Which government body in Tanzania is responsible for setting and checking the quality standards of goods?

options.text: Tanzania Bureau of Standards
Bank of Tanzania
Tanzania Ports Authority
Tanzania Revenue Authority

mcq.explanation: The Tanzania Bureau of Standards (TBS) sets quality standards and tests goods to protect consumers.

mcq.questionText: An advertisement that gives untrue information about a product in order to attract buyers is called

options.text: an informative advertisement
a misleading advertisement
a public advertisement
a competitive advertisement

mcq.explanation: Misleading advertisements deceive consumers by exaggerating or giving false claims about goods.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a responsibility of a consumer?

options.text: To buy goods without checking the quality
To ignore the expiry date of products
To demand and keep a receipt after buying
To accept any goods given by the seller

mcq.explanation: Keeping a receipt is a consumer responsibility because it serves as evidence of purchase when making a complaint.

mcq.questionText: Hiding goods in order to create artificial scarcity and raise prices is known as

options.text: hoarding
auctioning
warehousing
wholesaling

mcq.explanation: Hoarding is keeping goods out of the market to cause shortage so that prices rise, exploiting consumers.

mcq.questionText: The government weights and measures agency mainly protects consumers by

options.text: fixing the prices of all goods in shops
inspecting and verifying scales and measuring instruments
advertising goods to the public
importing goods for traders

mcq.explanation: The weights and measures agency checks that scales and measures are accurate so consumers get correct quantities.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best explains the importance of consumer associations?

options.text: They produce goods for consumers to buy
They unite consumers to defend their rights and raise their voice
They collect taxes from traders
They set the exchange rate for the currency

mcq.explanation: Consumer associations bring consumers together so they can demand fair treatment and report exploitation.

mcq.questionText: A trader sells a bag labelled '50 kg' but it actually contains only 45 kg. This trader is guilty of

options.text: offering a discount
giving false measure
providing credit
branding the product

mcq.explanation: Labelling 50 kg while giving only 45 kg is the use of false measures, which cheats the consumer.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the most effective way a consumer can protect himself when buying goods?

options.text: Buying from the seller with the loudest advertisement
Checking the expiry date, weight and quality before paying
Buying the most expensive item available
Refusing to ask any questions about the product

mcq.explanation: Inspecting expiry date, weight and quality helps a consumer avoid being exploited with poor or unsafe goods.

mcq.questionText: Why is the right to be informed important to a consumer?

options.text: It allows the consumer to refuse to pay for goods
It enables the consumer to make a wise choice based on true facts
It forces the seller to lower all prices
It removes the need for any advertising

mcq.explanation: The right to be informed gives the consumer correct information about price, quality and contents so a good decision can be made.

mcq.questionText: How does the Tanzania Bureau of Standards directly protect consumers from poor quality goods?

options.text: By giving loans to traders to buy stock
By testing goods and certifying those that meet required standards
By transporting goods from the factory to shops
By advertising goods on behalf of producers

mcq.explanation: TBS tests products and gives a quality mark to approved goods, helping consumers identify safe and standard products.

fib.questionText: A person who buys and uses goods and services to satisfy his or her needs is called a _____.
fib.explanation: The consumer is the final user of goods and services.

fib.questionText: Charging a buyer more than the correct price is a form of exploitation known as _____.
fib.explanation: Overcharging makes the consumer pay more than the fair value of the goods.

fib.questionText: Adding water to milk in order to increase its quantity is an example of _____.
fib.explanation: Adulteration is mixing genuine goods with inferior substances.

fib.questionText: The government body in Tanzania that sets quality standards for goods is the Tanzania Bureau of _____.
fib.explanation: The Tanzania Bureau of Standards (TBS) ensures goods meet required quality standards.

fib.questionText: An advertisement that gives false information to deceive buyers is called a _____ advertisement.
fib.explanation: Misleading advertisements give untrue claims that deceive consumers.

fib.questionText: The consumer right that protects buyers from goods that are dangerous to health is the right to _____.
fib.explanation: The right to safety guards consumers against harmful products.

fib.questionText: Hiding goods to create artificial shortage and push prices up is called _____.
fib.explanation: Hoarding causes false scarcity that raises prices to exploit consumers.

fib.questionText: Groups formed by consumers to defend their rights and report exploitation are called consumer _____.
fib.explanation: Consumer associations unite consumers to fight for fair treatment.

fib.questionText: A document given to a buyer as proof of purchase, useful when making a complaint, is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A receipt is evidence of purchase needed when claiming consumer rights.

fib.questionText: The use of inaccurate scales that give the buyer less than what is paid for is called false weights and _____.
fib.explanation: False weights and measures cheat the consumer by reducing the quantity received.

tf.questionText: A consumer is the final user of goods and services.
tf.explanation: A consumer buys and uses goods and services to satisfy needs.

tf.questionText: Overcharging means selling goods at a lower price than the correct price.
tf.explanation: Overcharging means selling at a higher price than the correct price.

tf.questionText: Adulteration of food can be harmful to the health of consumers.
tf.explanation: Adulteration adds inferior or harmful substances that can endanger health.

tf.questionText: The Tanzania Bureau of Standards is responsible for printing money in the country.
tf.explanation: TBS sets quality standards; printing money is the work of the Bank of Tanzania.

tf.questionText: Checking the expiry date before buying food is one way a consumer can protect himself.
tf.explanation: Checking expiry dates helps a consumer avoid buying spoiled or unsafe goods.

tf.questionText: Consumers have only rights and no responsibilities.
tf.explanation: Consumers also have responsibilities such as checking quality and keeping receipts.

tf.questionText: Misleading advertisements help consumers make correct buying decisions.
tf.explanation: Misleading advertisements deceive consumers and lead to wrong decisions.

tf.questionText: The government can protect consumers by inspecting weights and measures used by traders.
tf.explanation: Inspecting weights and measures ensures consumers receive the correct quantity.

tf.questionText: Hoarding goods to raise prices is a way of protecting consumers.
tf.explanation: Hoarding exploits consumers by creating shortage and raising prices.

tf.questionText: Consumer associations can help report and fight against consumer exploitation.
tf.explanation: Consumer associations unite consumers to defend their rights and report unfair practices.

summary.correctAnswer: A person who buys and uses goods and services to satisfy needs.
summary.explanation: The consumer is the final user in the chain of distribution.

summary.correctAnswer: Measures taken to safeguard consumers against exploitation by traders.
summary.explanation: It ensures consumers get fair quality, quantity and prices.

summary.correctAnswer: The right to safety from harmful goods and services.
summary.explanation: Other rights include the right to information and the right to choose.

summary.correctAnswer: Checking quality and keeping a receipt after buying.
summary.explanation: Responsible consumers verify goods and keep proof of purchase.

summary.correctAnswer: Selling goods at a price higher than the correct price.
summary.explanation: It is a common form of consumer exploitation.

summary.correctAnswer: Mixing genuine goods with inferior or harmful substances.
summary.explanation: For example, mixing water with milk to increase quantity.

summary.questionText: Role of the Tanzania Bureau of Standards
summary.correctAnswer: To set quality standards and test goods to protect consumers.
summary.explanation: It certifies goods that meet the required standards.

summary.questionText: Role of weights and measures inspection
summary.correctAnswer: To check that scales and measures are accurate.
summary.explanation: This ensures consumers receive the correct quantity they pay for.

summary.correctAnswer: To unite consumers and defend their rights against exploitation.
summary.explanation: They raise consumer awareness and report unfair practices.

summary.correctAnswer: Educating consumers about their rights and how to avoid exploitation.
summary.explanation: Other ways include government laws and quality control bodies.

hoq.questionText: A shopkeeper sells cooking oil that has passed its expiry date and removes the label so buyers cannot see the date. Which two consumer problems does this action create?

options.text: Fair pricing and free choice
Sale of unsafe goods and denial of the right to information
After-sales service and packaging
Good branding and quality control

hoq.explanation: Expired oil is unsafe, and hiding the date denies consumers true information needed to make a safe choice.

hoq.questionText: In a village market many traders use scales that read more than the actual weight. Which combined action would best protect the consumers?

options.text: Asking consumers to buy more goods than they need
Government inspection of weights together with consumer education on checking quantity
Allowing traders to set their own scales freely
Increasing the price of all goods in the market

hoq.explanation: Government inspection corrects the faulty scales while education helps consumers detect and report short measures.

hoq.questionText: A company runs a television advert claiming its drink 'cures all diseases', which is untrue. Why is this advert a serious threat to consumers and what body should act on it?

options.text: It is harmless, so no body needs to act
It misleads consumers into wrong health decisions, and standards or consumer protection bodies should act
It only affects the company, so the bank should act
It lowers prices, so the transport authority should act

hoq.explanation: False health claims can lead consumers to make dangerous decisions, so standards and consumer protection bodies must stop such adverts.
